draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Chidambaram! This is the home of Shiva as Nataraja, the cosmic dancer, and the walls of his temple show all 108 karanas from the Natya Shastra, the postures that underpin Bharatanatyam. The town's old name, Thillai, comes from the mangrove trees that still grow out at Pichavaram.
draft.hungryLine: The car streets around the temple are where to eat, with simple vegetarian meals on South and West Car Street and a non-veg spot if you want meat.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Head to the Thillai Nataraja Temple in the heart of town, with the Govindaraja Perumal shrine inside the same complex. Kezha Theru Mariamman Kovil is a 12 min walk from here.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Ride 13 km east to Pichavaram, where the mangrove forest is said to be the world's second largest.
moodReplies.surprise-me: It's the only Shiva temple that counts in both the Pancha Sabha Thalam and the Pancha Bhuta Thalam, and here Shiva is said to show himself as the sky.

legends.title: The dance duel
legends.body: Locals tell of a dance contest between Shiva and Kaali, one of the best known legends tied to Chidambaram. Along with Shiva's cosmic dance, it's a story you'll hear again and again here.

legends.title: The lost hymns found
legends.body: One of the town's best known stories is the rediscovery of the Tevaram hymns. It's a more recent legend than the cosmic dance, but just as loved.

tips.title: Catch Natyanjali in late February.
tips.body: This classical dance festival at the end of February draws thousands of people from all over the world.

tips.title: Expect huge festival crowds.
tips.body: During Margazhi Thiruvaadhirai in December to January and Aani Thirumanjanam in June to July, hundreds of thousands come to watch the procession and anointing.

story.title: Thillai forest
story.body: The town was first called Thillai, after the mangrove of Tillai trees that grow here and in the Pichavaram wetlands. A Shiva shrine already stood on the site back then.

story.title: Chola gold
story.body: The Cholas made the town their capital, renamed it Chidambaram and rebuilt the temple for their family deity, Nataraja. Parantaka I laid the golden tiled roof of the Chit Ambalam.

story.title: Kali on the outskirts
story.body: Chola King Kopperunchingan, who ruled in these years, built the Thillai Kali Temple at the edge of town.

story.title: Govindaraja returns
story.body: The Govindaraja idol had been uprooted from the complex under Kulothunga Chola II. King Krishnappa Nayak found it and put it back, and it's still one of the 108 Divya Desams.

story.title: A university town
story.body: Annamalai Chettiar founded Annamalai University in neighbouring Annamalai Nagar, now a 1,500 acre campus. Inside it, the old Chola-built Pasupatheswarar Temple was renovated in stone in 1914.
